## bf7ccb4288a7

**Reproduced canonical exclusion and seed-priority shortcut.**  Generator
SHA-256 `db3196396fa407db5e242426ac6524c71d7e75a3ffcfa8910259ee0d52f94ac5`;
executed rule hash `e214793e9a53`.

The target validator rejects canonical `train[0]` and `test[0]` with “at most
one marker may target each chamber,” although those canonical inputs deliberately
place two border seeds beside one chamber.  The Racket program resolves the
conflict by row-major processing: the first seed to flood the zero region wins.
A rival that processes border markers in reverse row-major order agrees with the
authority on `64/64` default generated samples (seeds `0..63`,
`sample_index = seed % 7`) because the generator never emits a conflict, but it
disagrees on canonical `train[0]` by filling the upper-left chamber with color 3
instead of color 2.  Evidence:
`checks/audit/bf7ccb4288a7/counterexample.json`,
`checks/audit/bf7ccb4288a7/canonical_racket.json`, and
`checks/audit/bf7ccb4288a7/generated_racket.json`.

The untouched battery failed lint, self-check, defect lint, profile floor, and
override checking; its summary is
`checks/audit/bf7ccb4288a7/battery/checks/bf7ccb4288a7_before_battery_summary.json`.
No audit-target fix was made.
